answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake. Each agent posts a bonded stake that is slashed if its answers are judged coherent but duplicated across accounts, so spinning up a thousand fake peers costs real capital. Peers are also sampled at random for each challenge, so an attacker cannot predict which nodes will grade them. A sparrow may be cheap to produce, but a glacier of locked stake takes time to melt, and a sonnet of varied, original replies is hard to forge at scale. Together these raise the price of every fake identity.
